args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Response: identified v2.3.0 as the most recent release that was healthy in production and rolled back to it. The initial rollback partially failed (orchestrator halted after us-east), leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1; a redeploy of v2.3.0 completed the rollout to all regions. Service is now healthy on v2.3.0 across all regions with a 0.2% error rate. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 regression and the orchestrator rollback failure.

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what happened and what I did:

**Situation:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.

**Actions taken:**
1. **Rolled back to v2.3.0** — the most recent release with a healthy production track record. The initial rollback partially failed (orchestrator error halted after us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1), so I completed the rollout by deploying v2.3.0 directly.
2. **Verified recovery** — all regions are now on v2.3.0 and healthy, with the error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.
3. **Opened a SEV2 incident** (INC-0001) describing the failure, the rollback (including the partial orchestrator failure), and follow-up items. It was created successfully despite a client timeout — I verified via the incident list before retrying, so there's only one incident on record and no duplicate page.

**Suggested follow-ups for the on-call/owners:** investigate the v2.3.1 regression and the orchestrator rollback failure that halted the rollout mid-way.
